config.footerNote: Original practice questions written to the published AQA GCSE Religious Studies A (8062) specification, using the question pattern for exams from June 2026 (1, 1, 4, 6 and 12 marks per theme, plus 3 SPaG marks on the 12-mark question). Not past-paper material. Model answers are indicative exemplars, not official AQA mark schemes; other valid answers are credited.

Theme A.1: 1-mark questions (AO1): either a multiple-choice question with four options (one correct letter) or a short 'Give one…' question. Only the first answer given is credited.
Theme A.4: 4 marks (AO1:3) – 'Explain two similar/different beliefs in contemporary British society about…' referring to the main religious tradition of Great Britain (Christianity) and one or more other religious traditions. For each belief: simple explanation of a relevant, accurate similarity/difference = 1 mark; detailed explanation = 2 marks. Required contrasting-belief issues for Theme A: contraception; sexual relationships before marriage; homosexual relationships.
Theme A.6: 6 marks (AO1) – 'Explain two religious beliefs about… Refer to sacred writings or another source of religious belief and teaching.' Each belief: simple explanation = 1 mark, detailed = 2 marks (×2). Source of authority: 2 marks for naming and applying a relevant source; 1 mark for naming it only, or applying it without naming it.
Theme A.12: 12 marks (AO2) – 'Evaluate this statement'. Levels of response: L4 (10–12) well-argued, reasoned consideration of different points of view, logical chains of reasoning leading to judgement(s), religion applied to the issue; L3 (7–9) reasoned consideration of different views with clear reference to religion; L2 (4–6) reasoned consideration of one view, or recognition of different views each supported by reasons (maximum Level 2 if no reference to religion); L1 (1–3) point of view with reason(s). Plus up to 3 SPaG marks (high 3 / intermediate 2 / threshold 1) for spelling, punctuation, grammar and range of specialist terms.

Theme B.1: 1-mark questions (AO1): multiple-choice (one correct letter from A–D) or 'Give one…'. Only the first answer is credited.
Theme B.4: 4 marks (AO1:3) – two similar/different beliefs in contemporary British society, referring to Christianity and one or more other religious traditions; each belief 1 mark simple, 2 marks detailed. Required contrasting-belief issues for Theme B: abortion; euthanasia; animal experimentation.
Theme B.6: 6 marks (AO1) – two religious beliefs (each 1 simple / 2 detailed) plus up to 2 marks for naming and applying sacred writings or another source of religious belief and teaching.
Theme B.12: 12 marks (AO2) – evaluate the statement: arguments for, arguments for a different view, religious arguments (maximum Level 2 without them), non-religious arguments optional, justified conclusion. L4 10–12, L3 7–9, L2 4–6, L1 1–3. Plus up to 3 SPaG marks.

Theme C.1: 1-mark questions (AO1): multiple-choice (one correct letter from A–D) or 'Give one…'. Only the first answer is credited.
Theme C.4: 4 marks (AO1:3) – two similar/different beliefs in contemporary British society. For Theme C the reference is to the main religious tradition of Great Britain (Christianity) and NON-RELIGIOUS beliefs such as atheism and humanism. Each belief 1 mark simple, 2 marks detailed. Required issues: visions; miracles; nature as general revelation.
Theme C.6: 6 marks (AO1) – two religious beliefs (each 1 simple / 2 detailed) plus up to 2 marks for naming and applying sacred writings or another source of religious belief and teaching.
Theme C.12: 12 marks (AO2) – evaluate the statement: arguments for, arguments for a different view, religious arguments (maximum Level 2 without them), non-religious arguments optional, justified conclusion. L4 10–12, L3 7–9, L2 4–6, L1 1–3. Plus up to 3 SPaG marks.

Theme D.1: 1-mark questions (AO1): multiple-choice (one correct letter from A–D) or 'Give one…'. Only the first answer is credited.
Theme D.4: 4 marks (AO1:3) – two similar/different beliefs in contemporary British society, referring to Christianity and one or more other religious traditions; each belief 1 mark simple, 2 marks detailed. Required contrasting-belief issues for Theme D: violence; weapons of mass destruction; pacifism.
Theme D.6: 6 marks (AO1) – two religious beliefs (each 1 simple / 2 detailed) plus up to 2 marks for naming and applying sacred writings or another source of religious belief and teaching.
Theme D.12: 12 marks (AO2) – evaluate the statement: arguments for, arguments for a different view, religious arguments (maximum Level 2 without them), non-religious arguments optional, justified conclusion. L4 10–12, L3 7–9, L2 4–6, L1 1–3. Plus up to 3 SPaG marks.

Theme E.1: 1-mark questions (AO1): multiple-choice (one correct letter from A–D) or 'Give one…'. Only the first answer is credited.
Theme E.4: 4 marks (AO1:3) – two similar/different beliefs in contemporary British society, referring to Christianity and one or more other religious traditions; each belief 1 mark simple, 2 marks detailed. Required contrasting-belief issues for Theme E: corporal punishment; the death penalty; forgiveness.
Theme E.6: 6 marks (AO1) – two religious beliefs (each 1 simple / 2 detailed) plus up to 2 marks for naming and applying sacred writings or another source of religious belief and teaching.
Theme E.12: 12 marks (AO2) – evaluate the statement: arguments for, arguments for a different view, religious arguments (maximum Level 2 without them), non-religious arguments optional, justified conclusion. L4 10–12, L3 7–9, L2 4–6, L1 1–3. Plus up to 3 SPaG marks.

Theme F.1: 1-mark questions (AO1): multiple-choice (one correct letter from A–D) or 'Give one…'. Only the first answer is credited.
Theme F.4: 4 marks (AO1:3) – two similar/different beliefs in contemporary British society, referring to Christianity and one or more other religious traditions; each belief 1 mark simple, 2 marks detailed. Required contrasting-belief issues for Theme F: status of women in religion; the uses of wealth; freedom of religious expression.
Theme F.6: 6 marks (AO1) – two religious beliefs (each 1 simple / 2 detailed) plus up to 2 marks for naming and applying sacred writings or another source of religious belief and teaching.
Theme F.12: 12 marks (AO2) – evaluate the statement: arguments for, arguments for a different view, religious arguments (maximum Level 2 without them), non-religious arguments optional, justified conclusion. L4 10–12, L3 7–9, L2 4–6, L1 1–3. Plus up to 3 SPaG marks.
